question: What is the primary purpose of home health care documentation?

options.A: To track the personal financial expenses of the client
options.B: To replace verbal communication among multidisciplinary team members
options.C: To serve as a legal account and ensure continuity of care
options.D: To provide marketing material for private home care agencies

explanation: Documentation acts as the official record of care delivered and ensures that different healthcare providers stay informed about the client's progress. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h1)

question: How does home health documentation fundamentally differ from acute hospital charting?

options.A: Home care documentation is entirely optional for registered nurses
options.B: Home care records often reside in the client's residence or travel with the nurse
options.C: Hospital records focus exclusively on social history rather than clinical data
options.D: Hospital charts require fewer legal signatures than home care notes

explanation: Because care occurs outside a central facility, the documentation physical setup must accommodate decentralized storage and transport. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h1)

question: Which regulatory body establishes the professional practice standards for Nigerian nurses?

options.A: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria
options.B: National Association of Nigerian Nurses and Midwives
options.C: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

explanation: The NMCN is the statutory body charged with regulating nursing education and practice in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h2)

question: What is the correct procedure when a charting error is made in a paper home health record?

options.A: Draw a single line through the mistake, date, sign, and write the correction
options.B: Tear out the affected page and rewrite the entire nursing note cleanly
options.C: Apply correction fluid generously over the error and write the new text
options.D: Obliterate the incorrect words completely with multiple heavy ink strokes

explanation: Crossing out an error with a single line preserves legibility, which is essential to maintain the legal integrity of the record. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h2)

question: Which item is essential to include in a Nigerian home health record due to local infrastructural challenges?

options.A: Vehicle registration plate of the visiting nurse
options.C: Serial number of the client mobile telephone
options.D: Detailed architectural blue print of the building

explanation: Precise landmarks are crucial for location tracking in areas where formal street naming and house numbering may be inconsistent. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h3)

question: Why must a home health medication profile explicitly document herbal remedies alongside prescribed drugs?

options.A: To screen for potential adverse herb-drug interactions
options.B: To determine the religious preferences of the family
options.C: To fulfill government agricultural reporting quotas
options.D: To calculate the monthly household food budget

explanation: Many clients combine orthodox medications with traditional herbs, which can significantly alter therapeutic drug efficacy or toxicity. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h3)

question: What does documenting psychosocial client needs primarily involve capturing?

options.A: Strict fluid input and output volumetric measurements
options.B: Caregiver strain, mental health indicators, and family dynamics
options.C: Physical range of motion limitations in the upper limbs
options.D: Exact biochemical lab values and radiological scan results

explanation: Psychosocial assessment focuses on mental, emotional, and social factors affecting the client and their support system. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h4)

question: A home care nurse notes that an elderly client lives alone in a poorly lit room with loose floor mats and no functional call system. What is the priority action regarding documentation?

options.A: Record these environmental hazards as fall risks to guide safety interventions
options.B: Omit the home environment details since clinical care focuses strictly on vital signs
options.C: Write a formal complaint about local municipal housing maintenance
options.D: Document only the client medical diagnosis and prescribed pill schedule

explanation: Documenting environmental hazards is essential in home care to formulate targeted interventions preventing client injury. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h4)

question: What does the evaluation phase of home health documentation primarily record?

options.A: The projected financial cost of future nursing visits
options.B: The academic qualifications of the attending nurse
options.C: The inventory count of remaining medical supplies
options.D: The client response and progress toward set goals

explanation: Evaluation measures whether the implemented nursing interventions successfully met the objectives outlined in the care plan. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h5)

question: Why is collaborative goal setting with the client and family important in home care documentation?

options.A: It eliminates the need for subsequent nursing progress notes
options.B: It legally transfers all medical liability away from the nurse
options.C: It fosters compliance and reflects realistic domestic capabilities
options.D: It guarantees complete financial reimbursement from the government

explanation: Goals established with client and family input are more achievable within the specific constraints of the home environment. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h5)

question: What style of language should be used when documenting client behavior for the multidisciplinary team?

options.B: Casual personal opinions and emotional labels

explanation: Objective notes focus on observable facts rather than subjective judgments, preventing bias among other team members. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h6)

question: What is the primary risk of poor interprofessional handover notes in home care?

options.A: Uncontrolled inflation of medical supply purchasing costs
options.B: Conflicting care instructions leading to client safety risks
options.C: Immediate termination of professional nursing licenses
options.D: Automatic deletion of historical client electronic files

explanation: When team members do not communicate clearly through documentation, contradictory interventions may be implemented, harming the client. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h6)

question: What is a practical strategy to prevent memory lapse when managing heavy home visit caseloads?

options.A: Asking family members to document the clinical nursing notes
options.B: Relying entirely on verbal memory until reaching the central office
options.C: Waiting until the end of the weekly shift to write all charts
options.D: Recording brief notes immediately after each client encounter

explanation: Immediate note-taking ensures accuracy and prevents details from being forgotten amidst subsequent visits. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h7)

question: Which challenge is most commonly associated with paper-based home health documentation in resource-limited environments?

options.A: Automatic synchronization errors across global server networks
options.B: High electrical power consumption during routine data entry
options.C: Physical vulnerability to weather elements, tearing, and loss
options.D: Frequent software update failures interrupting clinical workflows

explanation: Paper records carried in the field are susceptible to environmental damage, physical loss, and wear over time. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h7)

question: What legal maxim highlights the critical role of documentation in malpractice investigations?

options.A: Paper charts expire after twelve calendar months
options.B: Verbal witness accounts supersede written notes
options.C: Care not documented is care not done
options.D: Documentation is secondary to clinical intuition

explanation: This legal principle dictates that courts assume unrecorded care was never provided, regardless of verbal claims. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h8)

question: How do routine chart audits contribute to home health care delivery?

options.A: By increasing the financial taxes levied on private clients
options.B: By identifying documentation gaps and guiding quality improvement
options.C: By replacing direct supervisory observation of bedside skills
options.D: By punishing nurses for minor grammatical spelling errors

explanation: Audits systematically review records to spot systemic weaknesses, ensuring higher standards of care and documentation practice. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h8)
